title: Connections: Fork & Glass
desc: What links these foods? Spot the pattern, name the connection

questions.q: What connects: Champagne, Parmesan, Feta, and Darjeeling tea?
questions.a: They all have Protected Designation of Origin — they can only legally be called that if produced in their specific region

questions.q: What connects: a Bloody Mary, a Mimosa, and a Bellini?
questions.a: They're all brunch cocktails named after something else — a queen, a painter, and a cocktail

questions.q: Odd one out: Tofu, Tempeh, Seitan, Edamame. Which one and why?
questions.a: Seitan — it's made from wheat gluten, not soy. The other three are all soybean products

questions.q: True, false, or it depends: 'Sushi' means 'raw fish'
questions.a: False — sushi refers to the vinegared rice. Raw fish is 'sashimi'. You can have sushi with no fish at all

questions.q: Put these in order of Scoville heat units, mildest to hottest: Jalapeño, Habanero, Carolina Reaper, Tabasco sauce
questions.a: Tabasco (~2,500) → Jalapeño (~5,000) → Habanero (~300,000) → Carolina Reaper (~2.2 million)

questions.q: What connects: fortune cookies, chicken tikka masala, and Hawaiian pizza?
questions.a: None of them come from where you'd expect — fortune cookies are American, tikka masala is British, Hawaiian pizza is Canadian

questions.q: Name the dish: it originated in Cincinnati, contains chocolate and cinnamon in the sauce, and is served over spaghetti
questions.a: Cincinnati chili — a Greek-American invention nothing like Texan chili

questions.q: What's the connection: a roux, a slurry, and a beurre manié?
questions.a: They're all thickening agents for sauces — roux (fat+flour cooked), slurry (starch+cold liquid), beurre manié (raw butter+flour kneaded)

questions.q: Two of these are the same thing with different names. Which two? Coriander, Cilantro, Parsley, Culantro
questions.a: Coriander and cilantro — same plant (coriander is British English, cilantro is American). Culantro is a completely different herb

questions.q: What connects Vegemite, Marmite, and Bovril — and which is the odd one out?
questions.a: All are dark, salty spreads. Bovril is the odd one out — it's made from beef extract, while Vegemite and Marmite are yeast extract
